entries.title: Migration numbers follow ship order: identity 061; Phase C nominee 062, SIP 063, maturity 064

entries.title: Migration numbers: 061 identity, 062 investment email, 063 nominee, 064 SIP, 065 maturity, 066 audit index, 067 reviews
entries.text:
migrate.ts applies every unapplied file in filename order. To keep production order equal to filename order, numbers follow the plan's lanes:
- 061: A8 contact history (on main).
- 062: B1 investment_recorded email template check (on main).
- 063: C1 nominee (lane c-nominee).
- 064: C2 admin SIP schedules (lane c-sip).
- 065: C3 maturity schedule (maturity lane, after c-sip).
- 066: audit_events expression index on metadata userId for the per-client audit list (lane c-reports).
- 067: E1 client reviews (lane e-reviews).
- A bank reference on recordings (question row 16) and anything later take the next free number when built.
All of these ship in one release, so applying them out of order within it is harmless. Every new migration adds itself to the releaseUpgrade integration test's expected list; the coordinator merges the lists at landing. A migration that adds users columns must make earlier users-snapshot upgrade tests (userContactHistoryMigration) compare after their own migration only, as c-nominee did.

entries.title: Lane file rules: shared files that must not grow
entries.text:
- frontend admin adminQueries.ts must not grow: move the hooks a lane changes into its feature's own query module.
- packages/contracts/src/operations/admin-money.ts must not grow: new operations go in a new contract file per lane.
- backend_controller/src/runtime/composition.ts must not grow much: register new routes through a small composition module (adminComposition.ts, recordingComposition.ts).
- Generated OpenAPI and frontend operations are regenerated with the scripts at every rebase, never hand-edited.
Moved from the retired rule-7.

entries.title: Where each kind of record goes in this repository's tally
entries.text:
- Rules: only standing constraints agents must obey, short and imperative, each citing its source (RULES.md or a decision id). Only an operator session writes one.
- Decisions: everything the maintainer decided, in decisions.json (group admin-improvements), ids DEC-n, entered with the tally CLI decision add --operator. The plan's decision record carries the same DEC ids in its ID column.
- Questions: open choices with the conservative behaviour meanwhile. The plan's section 0a uses Q-0nn ids; the tally question text starts with the same Q-0nn. An answered question cites its DEC id (tally question answer ROW DEC-n).
- Findings: verified facts and defects. Conventions: how lanes work together. Howtos: commands.
- Plans, steps and progress stay in plans/admin-improvements.md; tasks, tracks, hand-offs, evidence and the ledger stay in tally.
Never put a decision or a question's answer in a rule entry (DEC-28).

entries.title: Where each kind of record goes in this repository's tally (phases, rule sections)
entries.text:
- Rules: only standing constraints agents must obey, each with a section (authority, safety, working, once) and a source (RULES.md or a decision id). Only an operator session writes one (context_put kind rule, or rule_tailor). RULES.md stays the rulebook; tally rules point at it or carry a maintainer constraint from a decision.
- Decisions: everything the maintainer decided, in decisions.json (group admin-improvements), ids DEC-n, entered with the tally CLI decision add --operator. The plan's decision record shows the same DEC ids.
- Questions: open choices with the conservative behaviour meanwhile; the tally text starts with the plan's Q-0nn id; an answered row cites its DEC id.
- Phases: each new stretch of work is a tally phase (phase_add, with its approving DEC id); its milestones use the phase id as stage. Stage `build` holds Phases A to G and the maintainer gates. Records commit once per phase (records.commitAt phase): phase_close commits them; records_commit only before the maintainer pushes mid-phase.
- Findings: verified facts and defects. Conventions: how lanes work together. Howtos: commands.
- Plans, steps and progress stay in plans/admin-improvements.md; tasks, tracks, hand-offs, evidence and the ledger stay in tally.
Never put a decision or a question's answer in a rule entry (DEC-28).

entries.title: Where each kind of record goes in this repository's tally (phases, rulebook)
entries.text:
- Rules (rulebook_get): only standing constraints, each with a section and a source. rule-16 points to RULES.md, the one rulebook; rule-17 and rule-18 carry maintainer constraints from decisions; rule-48 to rule-54 are tally's process rules tailored here (DEC-35). A template rule RULES.md covers stays retired. Only an operator session writes or tailors a rule.
- Decisions: everything the maintainer decided, in decisions.json (group admin-improvements), ids DEC-n, entered with the tally CLI decision add --operator; the plan's decision record shows the same ids.
- Questions: open choices with the conservative behaviour meanwhile; the tally text starts with the plan's Q-0nn id; an answered row cites its DEC id.
- Phases: each new stretch of work is a tally phase (phase_add with its approving DEC id); its milestones use the phase id as stage. Stage `build` holds Phases A to G and the maintainer gates. Records commit once per phase (records.commitAt phase): phase_close commits them on the maintainer's word; records_commit only before the maintainer pushes mid-phase.
- Findings: verified facts and defects. Conventions: how lanes work together. Howtos: commands.
- Plans, steps and close entries stay in plans/admin-improvements.md; tasks, tracks, hand-offs, evidence and the ledger stay in tally.
Never put a decision or a question's answer in a rule entry (DEC-28).
